description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

args.focus: Check against the change's spec delta (openspec/changes/implement-platform-foundation-ui/specs/platform-foundation/spec.md) and the store specs gamification ('Light and dark theme') and content-authoring (CA-D21). Pay attention to: the lint rule's false negatives (literal text it misses), whether the pseudo-catalog test can pass while a string bypasses the catalog, the theme and a11y e2e actually iterating every route, the provenance check's coverage of fixture/asset roots, nginx proxying and SPA fallback, the Dockerfile build with the contract submodule, and tsconfig splits leaking Node types into app code.

findings.title: Lint rule misses literal text passed through design-system text props (label, ariaLabel, kicker, legend, sr, …)
findings.evidence: `const TEXT_ATTRIBUTES = new Set(["aria-label", "title", "alt", "placeholder"]);` only covers DOM attribute names. Feature code is built from `@/design-system` components, which take their visible or accessible text through props such as `label?: string` (Icon becomes `aria-label={label}`, core.tsx:71), `ariaLabel` (Panel, core.tsx:126), `kicker`, `legend`, `meta`, `sr`, `show`/`hide` and `unit`. So `<Icon name="check" label="Hotovo" />` or `<Panel ariaLabel="Mise">` passes `npm run lint`. That breaks the spec requirement 'A lint rule SHALL refuse literal UI text in src/'. It also leaves out other DOM text attributes: `value` on submit inputs, `aria-description`, `aria-valuetext`, `aria-roledescription` and `aria-placeholder`.
findings.suggestion: Flip the default: report any string-literal JSX attribute value that contains a letter, and keep an allowlist of non-text props (className, id, data-*, type, name, role, href, lang, htmlFor, variant/tone/subject keys…). At minimum add the DS text props and the missing aria-* and value attributes. Add RuleTester invalid cases for `<Icon label="x"/>` and `<input type="submit" value="Odeslat"/>`.

findings.title: Lint rule misses literals inside conditional, logical, and interpolated template expressions
findings.evidence:
`isStringLiteral` accepts only a bare `Literal` or a `TemplateLiteral` with `expressions.length === 0`, and both visitors check only the top-level `node.expression`. So `

{done ? 'Hotovo' : t('x')}

`, `

{err && 'Chyba'}

`, ``

{`Úroveň ${n}`}

`` and `aria-label={open ? 'Zavřít' : 'Otevřít'}` are not reported. Neither are string constants rendered through a variable (`const L = 'Ahoj';

{L}

`) or strings in `.ts` modules, because the rule only runs on `src/**/*.tsx`. These are the most common ways literal UI text slips in.
findings.suggestion: Recurse into ConditionalExpression consequent/alternate, LogicalExpression right, and TemplateLiteral quasis (report if any quasi has a letter) for both children and text attributes. Rely on the pseudo-catalog render test as the backstop for variable indirection, and add RuleTester invalid cases for each shape.

findings.title: Pseudo-catalog test passes when literal text is concatenated after a catalog value
findings.evidence: The assertion is `texts.filter((t) => !t.startsWith('⟦'))`, and catalog values are only prefixed (`` `⟦${v}` ``). A text node built as `{t('a') + ' bodů'}`, ``{`${t('hero.level')} 3. úroveň`}`` or `aria-label={t('x') + ' close'}` begins with ⟦, so it passes even though part of the string bypasses the catalog. Separately, `visibleTexts` walks only `container`, so content portalled to `document.body` (dialogs, toasts) is never inspected. Its attribute list also omits `value` and the other aria-* text attributes.
findings.suggestion: Wrap each value as `⟦${v}⟧` and require every text node or attribute to be fully covered by one or more ⟦…⟧ segments (e.g. `/^(\s*⟦[^⟧]*⟧\s*)+$/`, allowing punctuation and digits between segments if interpolation is intended). Walk `document.body` instead of `container`, and add `value`, `aria-description` and `aria-valuetext`.

findings.title: App ignores the URL and always renders routes[0], so the 'every route' theme/a11y e2e cannot exercise real screens
findings.evidence: `<I18nProvider>{routes[0].element}</I18nProvider>` renders the first registered element regardless of `location.pathname`. The theme and a11y e2e loop over `ROUTE_PATHS`, and `routes.test.ts` only checks that `routes.map(r => r.path)` equals `ROUTE_PATHS`; nothing checks that navigating to a path renders that route's element. When a slice appends a second path before a router is wired, both e2e suites still go green while testing Shell twice. The coverage looks complete but isn't.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the element by path now, e.g. `routes.find(r => r.path === location.pathname)?.element` with a not-found fallback. Alternatively, have each e2e test assert a route-specific landmark or testid, so a path that does not render its screen fails.

findings.title: Pseudo-catalog test renders routes without app providers and only checks the first synchronous render
findings.evidence: `render(<I18nProvider messages={pseudo}>{route.element}</I18nProvider>)` mounts without `QueryClientProvider`, and asserts immediately. The first route that uses TanStack Query will throw ('No QueryClient set'). Text that only appears after data loads, in loading/error states or after interaction is never inspected. In practice the test checks the skeleton of each screen.
findings.suggestion: Render through a shared test wrapper with a QueryClient (and the router once it exists), with MSW or fixture data. Assert after `await findBy…`/`waitFor` settles, or add per-route states (loading, error, loaded) to the iteration.

findings.title: Provenance test checks only fonts/ and icons/; other asset roots are unguarded
findings.evidence: `const ASSET_ROOTS = ['src/design-system/fonts', 'src/design-system/icons'];` and `FIXTURE_ROOTS = ['fixtures', 'e2e/fixtures']`. Image, audio or PDF files under `public/`, `src/assets/`, `src/features/**`, `src/design-system/` outside those two folders, or `evals/cases/` (eval fixtures) are never scanned. A workbook scan or a copied mascot image dropped into `public/` or `src/assets/` passes the test, which defeats CA-D21/NFR-4. AGENTS.md also names `fixtures/self-authored/` as the PDF fixture home; that one is covered only because it sits under `fixtures/`.
findings.suggestion: Invert the scan: walk all git-tracked files (or `src`, `public`, `e2e`, `evals`, `fixtures`), select binary/media extensions (png, jpg, svg, webp, gif, woff*, ttf, otf, pdf, mp3, wav), and require each to be listed. Keep explicit roots only for the text fixtures.

findings.title: Spec's 'with its licence file listed' rule is not enforced
findings.evidence: For `licensed: <SPDX>` entries the test only checks `/^licensed: [A-Za-z0-9.+-]+$/` and `!isFixture`. The spec requirement says a licensed skin asset is listed 'with its licence file listed too'. A `licensed: OFL-1.1` font whose `*-OFL.txt` was deleted or never added still passes, as long as the font row itself exists.
findings.suggestion: Require at least one listed entry in the same directory, with the same SPDX id, whose file is a licence text (name matches /licen[cs]e|OFL|LICENSE/i). Alternatively, add a 'Licence file' column and check that it exists.

findings.title: Provenance manifest parser silently skips rows whose path is not backticked
findings.evidence: `.filter((l) => l.startsWith('| `'))` drops any table row written as `| e2e/fixtures/x.json | self-authored | … |`. Such a row is neither validated nor counted as listing the file. Coverage then fails with a confusing 'unlisted' message. Worse, a row with an invalid origin is never reported because it is never parsed. Separately, `existsSync` on Windows is case-insensitive, so a mis-cased path passes locally but fails on Linux CI.
findings.suggestion: Parse every table row after the header separator and fail on rows that do not match the expected shape. Compare listed paths case-sensitively against the `readdirSync` results instead of relying on `existsSync`.

findings.title: nginx proxy drops client IP and port; SPA fallback returns 200 HTML for missing assets
findings.evidence: `location /api/` sets only `Host $host` and `X-Forwarded-Proto`. `$host` strips the port, and no `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Real-IP`/`X-Forwarded-Port` is sent. The backend therefore sees nginx's IP for every request, which breaks any per-client throttling or logging. Origin/redirect checks behind a mapped port (e.g. localhost:8081) also see the wrong host. `try_files $uri /index.html;` also answers a missing `/assets/index-old.js` with 200 text/html. After a redeploy, a stale tab gets a MIME-type error instead of a 404. Without `Cache-Control: no-cache` on index.html, heuristic caching makes stale tabs more likely.
findings.suggestion: Use `proxy_set_header Host $http_host;` and add `X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`, `X-Forwarded-Port $server_port`. Configure Spring `server.forward-headers-strategy`. Add `location /assets/ { try_files $uri =404; expires 1y; }` and `add_header Cache-Control no-cache` for index.html.

findings.title: Docker build silently produces an image without the generated client if contract/ is absent
findings.evidence: `RUN npm run build` runs `tools/generate-api-client.mjs`. That script exits 1 only when `contract/` exists but is empty. If the directory is missing entirely (built from `git archive`/a tarball, or a context that omits the submodule), it falls through to `SKIP-pending` and exits 0, because `../docs` cannot exist inside the image. While no app module imports `schema.d.ts`, `tsc -b` still passes and the image ships with no contract pin check. The Dockerfile comment claims the image 'Builds from the pinned contract/ submodule'.
findings.suggestion: In the Dockerfile, assert the contract is present before building (`RUN test -f contract/api/openapi.yaml`), or pass an env flag (e.g. `API_GENERATE_REQUIRE_PIN=1`) that makes the generator fail instead of SKIP. Document `git submodule update --init` as a prerequisite in the compose docs.

findings.title: Node tsconfig now includes DOM lib for all Node-side files
findings.evidence: `"lib": ["ES2023", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"]` applies to `vite.config.ts`, `playwright.config.ts` and all of `e2e/`. Browser globals (`window`, `document`, `localStorage`) now type-check in Node-side code, where they throw at runtime. Only the `page.evaluate` callbacks actually need DOM types. In the other direction, the app/test split is sound: app files are still checked by tsconfig.app.json without `node` types. `tsconfig.test.json` re-includes all of `src` with node types, which only duplicates checking work.
findings.suggestion: Keep DOM out of tsconfig.node.json. Give e2e its own tsconfig (`tsconfig.e2e.json` with DOM) or add a narrow `/// <reference lib="dom" />` in the specs that use `page.evaluate`. Optionally limit tsconfig.test.json's include to `src/**/*.test.*` and `src/test` (app files are pulled in by imports).

findings.title: No-toggle check only detects switches and buttons with theme-ish names
findings.evidence: `page.getByRole('switch').or(page.getByRole('button', { name: /theme|motiv|tmav|světl|dark|light/i }))` does not catch a checkbox (`<input type=checkbox>` labelled 'Tmavý režim'), a radio group, a `<select>`, or an icon-only button labelled e.g. 'Režim'/'Vzhled'. The regex also gives false positives on legitimate buttons such as 'Highlight' or 'Spotlight'. The scenario 'no control on it switches between light and dark' is therefore only partially verified.
findings.suggestion: Assert behaviourally: click/toggle every interactive control on the route, then check that `html[data-theme]` is never set and the `--paper` background never changes. Alternatively, assert that no element sets `data-theme` and that no source file outside the design system references `data-theme` (unit/grep check).

findings.title: Reduced-motion e2e samples animations only at load, so later or interaction-triggered motion is never checked
findings.evidence: `document.getAnimations().filter((a) => a.playState === 'running')` runs once, right after `page.goto`. Animations started after hydration or data load (XP burst, mission reveal), or after an interaction, are never observed. CSS animations with a delay sit in 'pending'/'paused' at that instant and also pass. The test can therefore stay green while motion still plays under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
findings.suggestion: Wait for network idle or a route-ready marker before sampling. Also include `pending` animations and animations with a non-zero `effect.getTiming().duration`. Add interaction-driven checks once feature screens exist.

findings.title: Document title literal in index.html bypasses the catalog and both NFR-9 checks
findings.evidence: `<title>Doučko</title>` is a visible UI string (tab name, screen-reader announcement on load), but it is hard-coded. The lint rule only scans `src/**/*.tsx`, and the pseudo-catalog test never checks `document.title`. When admin routes arrive, their English title will have to bypass the catalog the same way.
findings.suggestion: Set `document.title` from the catalog in the shell/route (e.g. `t('app.name')`), and make the pseudo-catalog test assert `document.title.startsWith('⟦')`.

findings.title: Merging cs and en catalogs by spread silently overwrites colliding keys
findings.evidence: `export const messages = { ...cs, ...en };` merges the child and admin catalogs into one flat object. If both define the same key (e.g. `app.name`), the English value silently wins in the child UI, and nothing (type or test) catches it. The namespacing convention (`child.*` vs `admin.*`) is documented only in comments.
findings.suggestion: Add a unit test asserting the key sets of `cs` and `en` are disjoint and match their namespace prefixes, or type each catalog with a template-literal key type (`` `app.${string}` | `child.${string}` `` / `` `admin.${string}` ``).

findings.title: A failed real-name guard writes the child's real name into a committed QA report
findings.evidence: If `DOUCKO_CHILD_DISPLAY_NAME` is set and a page shows it, `expect(text).not.toContain(realName)` fails. Playwright then prints the expected substring (the real name) and the received body text. `scripts/qa-verify.mjs:331,370-372,431` copies each member's full stdout/stderr into `docs/qa/automated-verification-latest.md`, and that file is committed (it is in this diff). So the guard meant to keep the real name out of evidence is the thing that puts it into a tracked file, and from there into git history (NFR-3). The same text also goes into `playwright-report/` and the retained trace (`trace: 'retain-on-failure'`).
findings.suggestion: Don't hand the real name to a matcher that echoes it. Compute `const leaked = text.includes(name)` and call `expect(leaked, 'real display name appeared on page (NFR-3)').toBe(false)`. Optionally compare a hash. Also redact or skip e2e output that may hold body text before qa-verify writes the committed report.

findings.title: Real-name guard silently does nothing when the env var is unset, and the theme and a11y specs never call it
findings.evidence: `if (!realName?.trim()) return;` makes the guard pass when `DOUCKO_CHILD_DISPLAY_NAME` is absent. That happens in any shell that hasn't loaded the backend .env, which is the usual case for `npm run test:e2e`. `the e2e display name is fictional and distinct` also passes then, because `'Agent Nova' !== undefined`. `e2e/theme.spec.ts` and `e2e/a11y.spec.ts` load every route but never call `expectNoRealName`, even though the comment at profile.ts:11 says every spec that renders child screens does. Once child screens exist, recordings and traces can capture the real name with no failing check.
findings.suggestion: When running against the real stack (`externalBaseUrl` set), fail or print an explicit SKIP-pending line if `DOUCKO_CHILD_DISPLAY_NAME` is missing. Call the guard from a shared `test.afterEach` fixture so every spec gets it, rather than relying on each spec to opt in.

findings.title: nginx forwards no client IP, so backend login throttling sees every client as the proxy
findings.evidence: The `/api/` location sets only `Host` and `X-Forwarded-Proto`. It sets no `X-Real-IP` or `X-Forwarded-For`. If the backend throttles admin login by remote address (brute-force resistance, checklist item 2), every LAN device looks like the nginx container. A child's tablet or any guest device can then lock the parent out of admin by repeatedly failing logins, or the throttle has to be loose enough for all devices together, which weakens it. I could not confirm the backend's throttle key because ../backend was not readable in this session.
findings.suggestion: Add `proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;`. On the backend, trust these headers only from the nginx container (`server.forward-headers-strategy=native` plus a trusted-proxy restriction). Confirm the login throttle key in the backend review.

findings.title: No security response headers on the SPA or proxied API (nosniff, CSP, frame-ancestors, server_tokens)
findings.evidence: The server block sends no `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Content-Security-Policy`, `frame-ancestors`/`X-Frame-Options` or `Referrer-Policy`, and leaves `server_tokens` on. Later slices will serve uploaded PDFs/images (FR-1, FR-4) through this same `/api/` proxy and render task text. Without nosniff, a crafted upload served with a weak content type can be sniffed as HTML and run script in the admin origin. Without a CSP, any HTML-injection bug in task text becomes script execution. SameSite=Strict limits clickjacking of an authenticated admin, but nothing here forbids framing.
findings.suggestion: Add `server_tokens off;` and `add_header X-Content-Type-Options nosniff always;`. Add a CSP such as `default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; object-src 'none'` (check Vite's output for inline needs) and `Referrer-Policy no-referrer`. Keep the backend setting nosniff and `Content-Disposition` on downloads as well.

findings.title: Base images are floating tags, and nginx 1.27 is an old mainline branch
findings.evidence: `FROM node:22-alpine` and `FROM nginx:1.27-alpine` are mutable tags with no digest. The 1.27 mainline has been superseded, so a rebuild stays on a branch that may no longer get fixes, and the runtime image faces every device on the LAN. The final image also runs nginx's master process as root on port 80.
findings.suggestion: Pin both images by digest and move to a maintained nginx line. Consider `nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged` (listen on 8080) and update the compose mapping to match.

findings.title: no-literal-ui-text misses common ways to write literal UI text
findings.evidence:
The rule only checks JSXText, a bare string or no-expression template as a JSX child, and four attributes. All of these pass lint: `

{cond ? 'Hotovo' : t('x')}

`, `{done && 'Hotovo'}`, `{`Úroveň ${n}`}` (template with expressions), `const s = 'Ahoj';

{s}

`, ``, and `aria-description`, `aria-valuetext`, `aria-roledescription` or `label=`. Literal props passed to components also pass, e.g. `` or ``. So do `.ts` files (`document.title = 'Doučko'`) and `index.html` (`Doučko`). The spec scenario only covers `

Doučko

` and `aria-label`, so the RuleTester suite never tests these cases.
findings.suggestion: Check string literals inside ConditionalExpression, LogicalExpression and template quasis. Add `value` (on input/button), every `aria-*` text attribute, and `label`/`heading`/`text`-style props on capitalized components. Add RED invalid cases for each. Accept `index.html`'s title as a documented exception or set it from the catalog.

findings.title: Pseudo-catalog test passes when catalog text is concatenated with a literal, and only sees the first render state
findings.evidence: The assertion is `t.startsWith('⟦')` on each whole text node. So `{t('a') + ' navíc'}` or `{`${t('a')} – Ahoj`}` renders a single node `⟦… navíc`, which passes while the literal ' navíc' skips the catalog. Only `aria-label`/`title`/`alt`/`placeholder` are collected, so literals in `aria-valuetext`, `aria-description`, `value`, SVG `<title>` and `document.title` are never seen. Each route renders once, with no QueryClientProvider and no interaction, so loading, error, wrong-answer and dialog states are never checked. Routes that need query data will crash rather than be tested.
findings.suggestion: Wrap each catalog value in markers on both sides (`⟦…⟧`) and assert that each text node is made up entirely of wrapped segments. Collect every `aria-*` text attribute plus `value` and `document.title`. Render inside the same providers as `App` (QueryClient with mocked data). When stateful screens arrive, add per-state renders.

findings.title: Design-system components hard-code Czech strings that skip both the catalog and the lint rule
findings.evidence: `placeholder = 'Tvoje odpověď'` (line 63), 'Tvoje odpověď:' (78), 'Vyber všechny správné možnosti.' (100), 'Správně'/'Tohle ne' (109-110), 'Nahlásit problém' (45), and `aria-label="Zkušenosti do další hodnosti"` in game.tsx:44 are literals. `src/design-system` is in eslint `globalIgnores`, so the NFR-9 rule never sees them. When a feature slice renders these components, uncatalogued Czech reaches the child UI, and the English admin UI if reused there. Only the pseudo-catalog test could catch it, and only for the states it renders.
findings.suggestion: Raise this in the design-system artifact (not in a feature change): make every visible or accessible string a required prop, or read it from a strings context. Until then, feature code should always pass these props explicitly from `t()`.

findings.title: App ignores the URL, so the route-iterating theme and a11y e2e will pass for the wrong page once a second route is added
findings.evidence: `App` always renders `routes[0].element`, and nginx's `try_files $uri /index.html` serves the SPA for any path. `routes.test.ts` only checks that the `routes` and `ROUTE_PATHS` lists match. It does not check that the page at a path renders that route's element. When a slice adds `/admin` to both lists but forgets to wire a router, `theme.spec.ts` and `a11y.spec.ts` will load `/admin`, get the Shell, and pass. Admin screens behind login, and parameterized routes, will also need auth and params before the e2e reaches the real screen.
findings.suggestion: In each e2e test, assert a per-route marker (e.g. a `data-route` attribute or the route's h1 from the catalog) before running axe or the theme checks. When admin routes land, extend `ROUTE_PATHS` with how to reach each one (login fixture, sample params).

findings.title: Provenance check misses other asset roots and does not enforce the licence-file pairing
findings.evidence: `FIXTURE_ROOTS`/`ASSET_ROOTS` only cover `fixtures`, `e2e/fixtures`, `design-system/fonts` and `design-system/icons`. A workbook PDF, scan or answer-key JSON placed in `public/`, `src/assets/`, `evals/cases/`, `src/design-system/examples/` or `docs/` passes the test (NFR-4, CA-D21). The spec requires each `licensed:` asset to have 'its licence file listed too'. The test only checks the origin regex, so a font listed without its OFL text passes.
findings.suggestion: Scan every git-tracked file (`git ls-files`) whose extension is a binary/content type (pdf, png, jpg, svg, woff2, json under fixtures-like dirs) and require a manifest entry, or add `public`, `src/assets` and `evals/cases` to the roots. For each `licensed:` row, require another listed row in the same directory whose origin matches and whose name looks like a licence file.

findings.title: Checklist areas with no finding in this diff, and what was not verified
findings.evidence: Clean for this diff: (1) Authorization matrix: the diff adds no endpoints and no API calls; the generated client is unused so far. (2) Auth/sessions: nothing in scope; nginx proxies same-origin, so the SameSite=Strict cookie works. (3) Injection: no SQL, upload or HTML rendering yet; no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. SPA fallback via `try_files $uri /index.html` is fine, and `/api/` is matched first, so API 404s are not masked. (4) Exposure: no CORS config (same origin), so no `*`; I could not check the compose port binding because ../backend was not readable. (6) Secrets: no `VITE_*` variables; `.env`/`.env.*` are in .gitignore and .dockerignore; `npm ci --ignore-scripts` in the build. Dockerfile and contract: `api:generate` exits 1 if `contract/` exists without openapi.yaml, so an uninitialized submodule fails the image build instead of shipping without the client. tsconfig: `tsconfig.app.json` keeps `node` types out of app code. The broad `tsconfig.test.json` only adds a second check and loosens nothing. NOT verified: (7) Dependencies: `npm audit` was not run because the command was not approved in this session, so dependency risk is unassessed.
findings.suggestion: Run `npm audit` (and the backend's Maven advisory check) and fold the critical/high results into this review. Re-check compose port bindings (127.0.0.1 or a LAN IP, not 0.0.0.0) in the backend review.

findings.title: Coverage summary: 9 scenarios: 6 implemented, 3 partial, 0 missing, 0 contradicted
findings.evidence: Implemented: Dark OS, Light OS (e2e/theme.spec.ts:8-19), axe on every route (e2e/a11y.spec.ts:6-18), Smoke in three browsers (playwright.config.ts:21-25 + e2e/app-shell.spec.ts:6), Unlisted asset fails (src/test/provenance.test.ts:43-47), Real name on a page (e2e/app-shell.spec.ts:22-26). Partial: No toggle, Pseudo-catalog render, Literal text is a lint error (see the separate findings).
findings.suggestion: Close the three partial scenarios below. The OpenAPI boundary is clean: this slice calls no endpoints, and contract-client.test.ts checks that every contract path is in the generated schema.

findings.title: Lint rule misses common forms of literal UI text (conditionals, template literals, custom props, other ARIA attributes, .ts files)
findings.evidence:
Spec: "A lint rule SHALL refuse literal UI text in `src/`." The rule only reports a bare string Literal or an expression-free TemplateLiteral (isStringLiteral, line 12-14), and only for aria-label/title/alt/placeholder (line 10). It does not report: `{ok ? 'Ano' : 'Ne'}`, `{label ?? 'Zavřít'}`, `{`Ahoj ${name}`}`, `aria-label={x ? 'A' : 'B'}`, `

`, `aria-description`/`aria-roledescription`/`aria-valuetext`/`aria-placeholder`/`label`/`value` on input buttons, design-system props such as `
findings.suggestion: Walk ConditionalExpression/LogicalExpression branches and TemplateLiteral quasis. Add `children`, every `aria-*` text attribute, `label` and `value`. Treat string literals in props of PascalCase components as UI text unless allow-listed (className, variant, data-*, etc.). Extend files to `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}`. Add RuleTester invalid cases for each form.

findings.title: Pseudo-catalog test can pass while a string bypasses the catalog
findings.evidence: Spec: "THEN every visible text node and accessible name starts with `⟦`". The test checks only the prefix: `texts.filter((t) => !t.startsWith('⟦'))`. So `{`${t('a')} XP`}` or `t('a') + ' literal'` produce one text node `⟦… literal` and pass. It walks only `container` (line 12), so content portalled to document.body (dialogs, toasts) is never inspected. It reads only aria-label/title/alt/placeholder (line 17-18), missing `value` of input buttons, aria-description/aria-roledescription/aria-valuetext, and document.title. index.html:6 `<title>Doučko</title>` is a literal accessible name outside the catalog.
findings.suggestion: Make every pseudo value `⟦…⟧` and assert that each text node / attribute is made only of `⟦…⟧` segments (allowing whitespace and punctuation). Walk document.body, not container. Extend the attribute list. Set document.title from the catalog (e.g. in main.tsx/Shell) and assert it.

findings.title: Theme and a11y e2e iterate ROUTE_PATHS, but App ignores the URL, so every path renders the root screen
findings.evidence: Spec: "WHEN any route is opened … THEN the page background is the dark theme's --paper" and "axe on every route". App always renders `routes[0].element`. nginx (`try_files $uri /index.html`) and vite preview serve index.html for any path. As soon as a second path is added to ROUTE_PATHS/routes, e2e/theme.spec.ts:13 and e2e/a11y.spec.ts:11 will `goto(path)` and audit the root Shell, passing without ever rendering the new screen. Neither spec asserts that the expected route content is on the page. It is correct today only because there is one route.
findings.suggestion: Have each e2e assert a route-specific landmark or heading after goto (e.g. add `testId` to AppRoute). Or make App select the element by location.pathname now, so the registry and the rendered screen cannot diverge.

findings.title: No-toggle check is a name heuristic and misses non-button controls
findings.evidence: Scenario: "THEN no control on it switches between light and dark". The test only counts `role=switch` or buttons whose name matches /theme|motiv|tmav|světl|dark|light/i. A checkbox, radio, select/combobox, link or menuitem toggle, or an icon button named e.g. "Vzhled" or "Režim", would pass. The design system ships a `.dk-toggle` component (components.css:122).
findings.suggestion: Also make the assertion behavioural: activate each interactive control and check that `--paper` and `html[data-theme]` stay unchanged. Or at minimum add checkbox/radio/combobox/link roles and a `.dk-toggle` selector, plus more Czech terms (režim, vzhled).

findings.title: Provenance test does not enforce 'with its licence file listed too'
findings.evidence: Requirement: "Every skin asset SHALL be listed as `self-authored` or `licensed: <SPDX id>`, with its licence file listed too (NFR-4, CA-D21)." The test only checks that `licensed: X` matches /^licensed: [A-Za-z0-9.+-]+$/. Removing the `DelaGothicOne-OFL.txt` row and file would still pass, because nothing links a licensed asset to a listed licence file.
findings.suggestion: Add a column (or naming convention) that ties each licensed asset to its licence file, and assert that that file is listed and exists.

findings.title: Provenance roots omit Vite asset locations (public/, src/assets/) and the rest of the design system
findings.evidence: Scenario GIVEN: "a file under `fixtures/`, `e2e/fixtures/`, `src/design-system/fonts/` or `src/design-system/icons/`". Those roots are covered. But an image or PDF dropped into `public/`, `src/assets/`, `evals/cases/` or any `src/features/**` folder (the normal places for Vite static assets) is never checked, and missing roots are silently treated as empty (`files()` line 32). NFR-4's purpose (no workbook content) is broader than the four roots.
findings.suggestion: Amend the spec and test to scan `public/`, `src/assets/` and binary or image extensions anywhere under `src/` (outside generated code), or document why these roots are excluded.

findings.title: NFR-12 (generated client) is implemented and tested but has no requirement in the spec delta
findings.evidence: mvp-capability-plan.md:307 `| NFR-12 | platform-foundation | backend, frontend |`. tasks.md 2.4 and src/api/contract-client.test.ts (@trace NFR-12) implement it, but the delta has no `### Requirement` or scenario citing NFR-12. All other frontend-owned IDs (FR-58, NFR-3, 4, 6, 9, 13) appear.
findings.suggestion: Add a requirement like "Client generated from the pinned contract", with a scenario that every contract path is in the generated schema and that `build`/`typecheck` regenerate it.

findings.title: Scope drift: Dockerfile/nginx (SPA fallback, /api proxy, 51m body cap) and the reduced-motion check have no backing requirement
findings.evidence: The spec delta has no requirement for serving the SPA, proxying `/api/` to `backend:8080`, SPA fallback (`try_files $uri /index.html`) or `client_max_body_size 51m`. The only verification is the unticked manual task 4.4. Also: `/api` without a trailing slash and missing `/assets/*.js` both fall through to index.html with 200. `proxy_pass http://backend:8080` is resolved at nginx start, so nginx fails to boot if the backend container isn't resolvable yet. e2e/a11y.spec.ts:20-29 (reduced motion) is likewise not in the delta.
findings.suggestion: Amend the spec with a "Served behind one origin" requirement (SPA fallback, /api proxy → backend problem+json 404, upload limit) and a reduced-motion scenario under NFR-13. Add `location /assets/ { try_files $uri =404; }` and a resolver/variable upstream or a compose healthcheck dependency.

findings.title: Dockerfile comment claims regeneration from the pinned contract but does not guard an absent submodule
findings.evidence: Dockerfile:1-2 says "Builds from the pinned contract/ submodule: api:generate regenerates the client inside the image (NFR-12)". `COPY . .` copies whatever is on disk. If `contract/` is absent (clone without --recursive and no dir), tools/generate-api-client.mjs:24 prints `SKIP-pending` and the build continues without the pinned contract. An empty, uninitialized dir does fail (line 20-21). The image therefore isn't guaranteed to be built from the pin.
findings.suggestion: Add `RUN test -f contract/api/openapi.yaml` before `npm run build`, or make api:generate fail when it runs in CI/Docker (e.g. when `CI` or a `REQUIRE_CONTRACT` env var is set).

findings.title: tasks.md checkboxes don't reflect delivered artifacts
findings.evidence: Every task is `[ ]`, but the artifacts for 2.1-2.7 and 3.1-3.6 exist in this diff (i18n-coverage.test.tsx, lint-rule.test.ts, provenance.test.ts, contract-client.test.ts, theme/a11y/app-shell e2e, src/i18n, routes.tsx, eslint rule, playwright projects, PROVENANCE.md, Dockerfile, nginx.conf). No ticked-without-artifact violations, but the inverse drift hides progress. 2.8 (RED observed) has no evidence pointer.
findings.suggestion: Tick 2.1-2.7 and 3.1-3.6. Tick 2.8 only with a pointer to the recorded RED run. Leave 4.x unticked until qa:verify and the review gate produce evidence.

findings.title: Merged catalog lets English silently shadow Czech; nothing enforces child=cs, admin=en
findings.evidence: Spec: "Czech for the child UI and English for the admin UI (NFR-9)." `export const messages = { ...cs, ...en };`: if a key exists in both catalogs, the en value overrides cs without any error. The `app.*`/`child.*` vs `admin.*` namespaces are only a comment convention, and no test checks that child routes draw only from cs.
findings.suggestion: Type each catalog's keys with a namespace prefix (e.g. `Record<`admin.${string}`, string>` for en) or add a unit test asserting disjoint keys and correct prefixes.

findings.title: tsconfig split is sound: Node types do not leak into app code (no defect)
findings.evidence: tsconfig.app.json has `types: ["vite/client"]` and excludes tests and src/test. tsconfig.test.json re-includes `src` with `node` types, but only in its own project. App files are still type-checked once by the app project without Node globals, so `process`/`fs` in app code fails `tsc -b`. tsconfig.node.json covers e2e and configs only. One residual risk: helpers placed in `src/test/` are compiled only with Node types, and an app file importing them would not be flagged by the app project.
findings.suggestion: No change needed. Optionally add an ESLint `no-restricted-imports` rule that blocks `src/test/**` and `node:*` imports from non-test src files.

The design-system components really do take visible or accessible text through other prop names:
- **Icon:** `label?: string` (`core.tsx:66`) is rendered as `aria-label`.
- **Panel:** `ariaLabel` (`core.tsx:121`/`126`) is rendered as `aria-label`, and `kicker` is rendered as visible text (`core.tsx:127`).
- **TaskPrompt:** `kicker` and `power` (`practice.tsx:14`).
- **Answer input:** `label` (`practice.tsx:59`).
- **Choice group:** `legend` (`practice.tsx:86`).

The design system's own example even passes literals this way: `kicker="Úloha 4/10" power="Desetinná čísla"` (`TaskScreenExample.tsx:21`). The same pattern in feature code would pass lint.

Nothing else catches it. The `JSXExpressionContainer` handler deliberately skips containers whose parent is a `JSXAttribute`, and the `JSXText` handler only sees children.

`<Panel title="...">` happens to be caught, but only because `title` matches the DOM attribute name.

This contradicts the change spec, which says the lint rule SHALL refuse literal UI text in `src/` (`openspec/changes/implement-platform-foundation-ui/specs/platform-foundation/spec.md:30`). It also misses DOM text attributes such as `value` on submit inputs and `aria-valuetext`.

I confirmed the mechanism in `nginx.conf:10-18`. The image is built from this file (`Dockerfile:11` copies it to conf.d/default.conf).

(1) The `/api/` location sets only `Host $host` and `X-Forwarded-Proto`. `$host` is the request host without the port, and there is no X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP or X-Forwarded-Port. So every proxied request reaches the backend with nginx's container IP as its peer address, and the original port is lost.

(2) `try_files $uri /index.html` falls back to an internal redirect to /index.html for any missing URI, including /assets/*.js. That returns 200 text/html, and a browser enforcing module MIME types rejects it. A 404 would be correct.
